name: vehicle
description: Something that carries people or goods from one place to another.
conventions: A vehicle is longest along z, so its length is z, its width x and its height y.
anticipate: A driver or cockpit position and camera point.
Lights (head, tail, brake) as separate emissive parts or nodes.
Collision as a simple box or convex hull around the body.

name: wheeled vehicle
description: A vehicle on wheels.

parts.name: Wheel
parts.note: Spins about the axle (x). Front wheels also steer about y: add a Steer pivot node above the wheel node.

anticipate: Wheel nodes with the pivot at the hub, so they can spin and steer.
Suspension travel: the body and wheels are separate nodes.
pitfalls: Wheels merged into the body, or with the pivot at a corner, cannot spin.
Wheels that do not touch y = 0 make the vehicle float or sink.

name: car
description: A passenger car.

parts.name: Wheel
parts.note: Front wheels also steer about y.

parts.name: Glass
parts.note: Windscreen and windows, as a separate transparent material.

parts.name: Door
parts.note: Hinged at the front edge, about a vertical axis.

parts.name: SteeringWheel
parts.note: Inside the cabin; the pivot is the column axis.

scale.source: general knowledge: typical production range, not a standard for passenger cars (city car to large SUV); wheel diameter about 0.55-0.80 m

anticipate: Wheelbase about 55-60% of the length; wheels near the corners.
Four wheel nodes named by position (Wheel_FL, Wheel_FR, Wheel_RL, Wheel_RR); the front ones steer.
pitfalls: Boxy 'brick' cars read as toys: give the body a loft with a tapered nose and tail.
Glass and body in one material cannot be transparent.

name: truck
description: A lorry or goods vehicle.

parts.name: Wheel
parts.note: Dual rear wheels count as separate nodes; only the front axle steers.

parts.name: Trailer
parts.note: Coupled at the fifth wheel; pivot at the coupling.

scale.source: EU Directive 96/53/EC limits 2.55 m width and 16.5 m articulated length; other sizes are general knowledge

pitfalls: Trailers must be separate nodes with a pivot at the coupling, or they cannot swing.

name: bus
description: A road bus or coach.

parts.name: Door
parts.note: Folding or sliding passenger doors.

scale.source: EU limits: 2.55 m width, 18.75 m articulated length; heights are general knowledge

name: motorcycle
description: A motorbike or scooter.

parts.name: WheelFront
parts.note: Steers with the fork: put it under the Fork node.

parts.name: Fork
parts.note: Rotates about the steering axis, which leans back about 25-30 degrees.

scale.source: general knowledge: typical production range, not a standard; wheel diameter about 0.5-0.7 m

pitfalls: The steering axis is tilted, not vertical: a vertical pivot makes the front wheel wobble sideways.

name: bicycle
description: A pedal bicycle.

scale.source: general knowledge: typical production range, not a standard; wheels 26-29 inch (about 0.66-0.73 m)

name: tractor
description: A farm tractor.

parts.name: WheelRear
parts.note: The large pair, about 1.4-2.1 m diameter.

parts.name: WheelFront
parts.note: The smaller pair, about 0.8-1.4 m diameter; they steer.

parts.name: Hitch
parts.note: Three-point linkage at the rear.

scale.source: general knowledge: typical production range, not a standard; EU road width limit is 2.55 m

pitfalls: Rear wheels are much larger than the front ones: equal wheels look like a toy.

name: tracked vehicle
description: A vehicle that runs on tracks.

parts.name: Track
parts.note: Animate by scrolling the track texture; the road wheels spin.

pitfalls: Tracks modelled as a single solid slab cannot show motion: use a texture offset or separate link nodes.

name: tank
description: A battle tank.

parts.name: Turret
parts.note: Rotates about the vertical axis through the turret ring.

parts.name: Gun
parts.note: Elevates about the trunnion, a horizontal axis in the turret; recoil slides along z.

scale.source: general knowledge: typical production range, not a standard; the low end is the hull, the high end includes a forward-pointing gun

pitfalls: A gun fused to the turret cannot elevate: the turret, gun and mantlet are separate nodes.

name: rail vehicle
description: A vehicle that runs on rails.

parts.name: Bogie
parts.note: Carries the wheelsets; pivots under the body.

anticipate: Standard gauge is 1.435 m between the rail heads (UIC/IEC standard), so the wheelsets sit about 1.5 m apart (x).

name: train
description: A locomotive, railcar or train.

scale.source: general knowledge: typical production range, not a standard for a single locomotive or railcar; UIC maximum width is about 3.15 m

pitfalls: Wheelsets that do not sit on the rails (1.435 m gauge) float or clip: check the wheel positions.

name: high-speed train
description: A train for 250 km/h and more: streamlined end cars, pantographs and often articulated bogies.

scale.source: general knowledge: one end car or power car; a full set is about 200 m long

pitfalls: At 80-100 m/s, streaming and trackside objects must be placed ahead along the line, and the track profile needs large vertical curves.
Synthesised motor tones that rise with speed become a whine above about 1 kHz; cap the pitch.

name: rack railway car
description: A mountain railway car that climbs steep grades with a cog wheel in a rack between the rails.

scale.source: general knowledge: metre-gauge rack railcars are about 15-17 m long, on grades of up to about 25 %

pitfalls: A train on a rack must not roll back when the brakes are released on a grade.
Far from the origin, drive bogies and wheels by local transforms from cached rest values, not by writing global transforms.

name: fire engine
description: A fire service truck: a pumper with lockers, hose reels and a pump, or an aerial ladder truck.

parts.name: Ladder
parts.note: On a turntable over or behind the rear axle; sections slide out along the ladder.

scale.source: general knowledge: two-axle pumpers and 30 m class ladder trucks; width without mirrors is at most 2.55 m in the EU

pitfalls: The cab is narrower than the body behind it; roller shutters must not run through the wheel arches.
A ladder truck deploys its outriggers before the ladder may rise.

name: ambulance
description: An emergency ambulance: a van or light-truck cab with a box-shaped patient compartment behind it, warning lights, and rear and side doors.

parts.name: Body
parts.note: The box behind the cab, wider and taller than the cab.

parts.name: Wheel
parts.note: Twin rear wheels on heavier chassis. Spins about the axle (x); the front pair also steers about y.

parts.name: Door
parts.note: Cab doors hinge at the front edge, the rear doors at the outer edges; the side door often slides.

parts.name: SteeringWheel
parts.note: Inside the cab; the pivot is the column axis.

scale.source: general knowledge: box ambulances on Mercedes-Benz Sprinter, Fiat Ducato or Ford E-Series chassis are about 6-7.5 m long, the box about 2.1-2.4 m wide and the roof 2.7-3.1 m high

options: US type I on a truck chassis
US type III on a van chassis

anticipate: Flashing warning lights as separate emissive nodes, so a script can blink them.
Rear doors hinged at the outer edges for loading a stretcher; a step at the rear.
pitfalls: The box is wider than the cab: a box flush with the cab doors looks like a plain van.
Mirror-reversed lettering on the bonnet is only for the front; do not mirror it on the sides.

name: forklift
description: A counterbalance forklift truck: a short chassis with a heavy counterweight at the rear, an overhead guard over the driver, and a tilting mast at the front with a carriage and two forks that lift.

parts.name: Wheel
parts.note: Large drive wheels under the mast, smaller steered wheels under the counterweight (the rear wheels steer).

parts.name: Mast
parts.note: Tilts about x on the pins at its foot (about 6 degrees forward, 6-12 back); the inner channels and the carriage slide up inside it.

parts.name: Carriage
parts.note: Carries the forks and the load backrest; slides up the mast.

parts.name: Fork
parts.note: About 1.0-1.2 m long, level with the ground when lowered.

scale.source: general knowledge: 1.5-3.5 t counterbalance trucks (Toyota, Linde, Jungheinrich data sheets) are about 2.1-2.8 m long to the fork face plus 0.9-1.2 m of forks, 1.0-1.3 m wide, with the overhead guard about 2.1-2.2 m high and the lowered mast 2.0-2.5 m

anticipate: The carriage as its own node with the pivot at its base, so a script can lift the forks by moving it up y.
Mast tilt about its foot pin (x), a few degrees forward and back.
pitfalls: The forks must be level and touch the ground when lowered, not float in front of the mast.
The steered wheels are at the rear, under the counterweight.

name: excavator
description: A crawler excavator: an undercarriage with two tracks, an upper structure that slews on a turntable with the cab, engine and counterweight, and a digging arm of boom, stick and bucket moved by hydraulic cylinders.

parts.name: Hull
parts.note: The lower frame between the tracks.

parts.name: House
parts.note: Slews about the vertical axis through the centre of the slewing ring, on top of the undercarriage; the arm is its child.

parts.name: Boom
parts.note: Pivots about x at its foot pin on the upper structure; the stick and bucket are its children.

parts.name: Stick
parts.note: Pivots about x at the boom tip.

parts.name: Bucket
parts.note: Pivots about x on its pin at the stick tip; teeth on the cutting edge.

scale.source: manufacturer data: 20 t class crawler excavators (Cat 320, Komatsu PC210) are about 9.5 m long in transport position, 2.8-3.2 m wide over the tracks and 3.0 m high at the cab; with the boom raised the arm reaches 6-7 m

anticipate: The house, boom, stick and bucket as a chain of nodes, each with its pivot on its pin, so a script can dig.
Hydraulic cylinders that follow the arm: aim them at their far pin every frame (lookAt) or give them a slide node.
pitfalls: The cab sits on the left of the boom, the engine and counterweight at the back.
The house slews on the centre of the undercarriage, not on the middle of its own box.

name: tram
description: A low-floor articulated city tram: several short carbody sections joined by bellows, with a cab at each end, wide double doors, large windows and a pantograph; bogies sit under some sections, the others hang between them.

parts.name: Body
parts.note: One node per carbody section.

scale.source: general knowledge: low-floor trams such as the Siemens Combino, Alstom Citadis and Bombardier Flexity are 2.3-2.65 m wide, 20-45 m long in 3-7 sections and about 3.4-3.6 m high to the lowered pantograph; floor about 0.35 m above the rail

anticipate: Each section its own node, so a script can bend the tram through a curve at the articulations.
Doors as sliding nodes (plug doors move out and along z).
pitfalls: A low-floor tram has its floor about 0.35 m above the rail: a body on top of the bogies looks like a train.
Sections without a bogie hang between their neighbours; do not give every section wheels.

name: go-kart
description: A racing kart: a low tubular steel frame without suspension, four small wheels, a bucket seat, a steering column, a small engine beside the seat, and plastic nose, side pods and rear bumper.

parts.name: Wheel
parts.note: Rear tyres are wider than the front ones; the rear axle is solid. Spins about the axle (x); the front pair also steers about y.

scale.source: CIK-FIA technical regulations for karts: overall length at most 2.1 m, overall width at most 1.4 m, height at most 0.65 m from the ground without the driver; wheelbase 1.01-1.07 m

anticipate: A driver position low between the side pods, legs forward to the pedals.
Front wheels steer about a kingpin each (y), the rear axle spins as one.
pitfalls: A kart has no suspension and no body over the wheels: the wheels stand free beside the frame.
The engine sits to the right (or left) of the seat, driving the rear axle by a chain.

name: horse-drawn carriage
description: A horse-drawn carriage or coach: a sprung body on four wooden spoked wheels, larger at the rear, with a driver's box at the front and shafts or a pole for the horse. Closed coaches have a roof, doors and windows; open ones a folding hood.

parts.name: Wheel
parts.note: Wooden spoked wheels with an iron tyre; the front pair is smaller and turns with the front axle (a fifth wheel).

parts.name: Shaft
parts.note: Two shafts for one horse, or a single pole between a pair.

parts.name: Axle
parts.note: The front axle turns about y to steer.

scale.source: general knowledge: a coach body is about 2-3 m long on wheels of 0.9-1.5 m diameter; with the shafts the carriage is about 4.5-6 m long, 1.6-2 m wide over the hubs and 2.2-2.8 m high when closed

anticipate: An attachment point at the shaft tips for a horse model (the horse stands between the shafts).
The front axle as its own node that turns about y to steer.
pitfalls: The rear wheels are larger than the front ones; equal wheels look like a cart.
The shafts are level with the horse's shoulders, about 1-1.2 m above the ground at their tips.

name: hovercraft
description: An air-cushion vehicle: a buoyant hull on a flexible skirt filled by lift fans, driven over land and water by ducted propellers at the stern with rudders behind them.

parts.name: Skirt
parts.note: Rubberised fabric around the hull; it touches the ground when the craft is at rest.

scale.source: builder data: the Griffon 12000TD on the Solent is about 22 m long and 10.5 m wide, the BHT130 about 30 m by 12 m, the SR.N4 Mk III was 56.4 m long and 23.2 m wide

anticipate: Propellers as separate nodes with the pivot at the hub, spinning about z.
The craft rises about 1-2 m on its cushion when running: move the whole model up, the skirt stays its shape.
pitfalls: A hovercraft rests on its skirt on y = 0; it has no keel below the waterline like a boat.
The propellers push air backwards: they sit at the stern, facing -z, with the rudders behind them.
